text: The Patriots bid farewell to one of the greatest defensive backs in franchise history this week as Stephon Gilmore, the 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year and two-time All-Pro, signed a one-day contract to retire as a member of New England, cementing his legacy among the team's all-time cornerbacks. On the injury front, running back TreVeyon Henderson has declared himself "ready to go" for Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Steelers after missing the opener with an ankle injury, though New England could be without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who is officially questionable heading into the contest. The Patriots are looking to bounce back after their opener as they face a rolling Steelers team in what figures to be a telling early-season test for Drake Maye and the offense, while the organization continues its promotional efforts for the upcoming Munich game with Adam Vinatieri—the Pro Football Hall of Fame placekicker—attempting a Guinness World Record kick in the Swiss Alps.
